mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, تبتغي: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in تحرم.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying تَحِلَّة: accusative by فرض. Its pattern is تَفْعِلة, and its origin is تَحْلِلة; then the vowel of the first lām was transferred onto the حاء and [the lām] was assimilated into the second.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying نبأت بِهِ: the object is omitted, its implied form being "she informed her companion of it" (نبأت به صاحبتها), meaning ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa, may Allah be pleased with them both; Ḥafṣa was the one who told ʿĀʾisha the secret. Likewise the object is also omitted from His saying, Exalted is He, عرف بعضه, in the reading of whoever doubles the رآء, i.e. "he made her acquainted with part of it", i.e. part of what she had disclosed to her companion, "and turned away from part", out of generosity on his part ﷺ, so he did not make her acquainted with it. As for whoever reads the رآء without doubling [عَرَف], it is in the sense of "he requited part of it and did not requite part", out of kindness on his part ﷺ. It is not good for its meaning to be that he did not know part of it, because Allah has told us that He made His Prophet aware of it; so it is not possible that He made him aware of what she disclosed and he knew part of what He made him aware of and not another part, or knew part and was ignorant of part.
His saying فإن الله هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ: هو is a separating pronoun (fāṣila), and مولاه is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. It is also possible that هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مولاه the khabar, the clause being the khabar of إنّ; on this view you pause on مولاه and do not go beyond it.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying قُلُوبكُمَا: القلب was put in the plural, although they are two, only because anything of which there is only one in a person, when its like is joined to it, is [expressed as] a plural. It is also said: because the dual is a plural, since it is the joining of one thing to another.
His saying وَجِبْرِيل: a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is conjoined to it, and ظهير is the khabar (predicate). It is also possible that وجبريل is conjoined to مولاه, المولى meaning the protecting friend (الولي); on this view you pause on جبريل, and وصالح المؤمنين is a mubtadaʾ, والملائكة is conjoined, and ظهير is the khabar. It is also possible that وصالح المؤمنين is conjoined to جبريل, and جبريل conjoined to مولاه, المولى meaning the protecting friend, because the angels and the believers are the protecting friends of the prophets and their helpers; on this view you pause on المؤمنين, and His saying والملائكة is a mubtadaʾ and ظهير its khabar. However, what is customary among the readers is to pause on مولاه, and جبريل is a mubtadaʾ with which one begins.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying أَن يُبدلهُ: أن is in the position of the accusative, the khabar (predicate) of عسى; like it is أن يكفر.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying قوا أَنفسكُم: قوا is a verb whose first and third radicals are both weak. The first radical (fāʾ) is omitted because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra in your saying يقي, according to the doctrine of the Basrans. The Kufans said it was only omitted to distinguish between the transitive and the intransitive verb: so it was omitted in يعد and يقي because they are transitive, and kept in يوجل because it is intransitive. But it follows for them that they should not omit it in يرم and يثق, because they are intransitive, while omission is necessary in both. The third radical (lām) is omitted because it is quiescent and the wāw after it is quiescent. The nūn is omitted because of indeclinability (bināʾ) according to the Basrans, and because of the jussive according to the Kufans. Its origin is أوقيوا; the wāw was omitted for the reason we mentioned, so the connective alif was dispensed with; then the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred onto the قاف, and [the yāʾ] was omitted because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent, so it became قوا. It is also said, rather, that the ḍamma was removed from the yāʾ for lightness, and [the yāʾ] was omitted because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent, and the قاف was given a ḍamma for the sake of the wāw, so that it would not change into a yāʾ and the meaning be altered. Parallels to this have preceded.
His saying وَمَرْيَم ابنت عمرَان: مريم is accusative by conjunction with مثلا, and ابنة is a naʿt (adjective) of it or a badal (substitute). مريم is a diptote because of femininity and definiteness. It is said that it is a foreign (non-Arabic) noun, and it is also said that it is Arabic.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying ضرب الله مثلا للَّذين كفرُوا امْرَأَة نوح وَامْرَأَة لوط: [مثلا and امرأة نوح are] the two objects of ضرب. It is also said that امرأة نوح is a badal (substitute) of مثل, on the assumption of "the likeness of the wife of Noah" (مثل امرأة نوح); then the second مثل was omitted because the first indicates it.
